lines.text: These twin sisters were born in Room 4 of the maternity ward, on one autumn night.
Ivy came first, at exactly 1:55 in the morning. Twenty-five minutes later, her sister June arrived.
Ivy is the big sister. Everybody agrees.
Nurse Hana writes the birth certificates at the nurses' station, and she checks every time twice.
Then she reads them back, and something strange happens.
Ivy, born 1:55 AM. June, born 1:20 AM.
On paper, the younger twin came first. So every birthday, the older twin blows out her candles second.
Hana checks again. No typo. Same room, same night, same clock on the wall.
So how was the younger twin born before her big sister?
You have ten seconds. Comment your answer now.
The answer was hanging on the ward wall all night.
It was the first Sunday in November, and at 2 AM, the clocks went back one hour.
Ivy arrived at 1:55. Five minutes later, two o'clock turned back into one o'clock.
June arrived twenty minutes after that, at 1:20, the second time the clock showed it.
Twenty-five minutes younger, but thirty-five minutes older on paper.
Hana laughs so hard she drops her clipboard.
Ivy is older. June has the paperwork. They still argue about it every birthday.
So, did you get it right? Follow for more.
